subject: Re: Dedicated GPU capacity deep-dive — confirm availability
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@orionbiotech.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@orionbiotech.com>
Date: 2026-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated GPU architecture review request

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo earlier — the team at Orion is very interested in moving to a dedicated Redwood capacity model for our inference pipelines. We'd like to schedule a technical deep-dive next week focused on pool sizing, autoscaling behavior, and workload isolation (multi-tenant vs. tenant-isolated pools).

Proposed attendees from our side:
- Elena Morales (Ops)
- Arjun Patel (Platform/infra)
- two members from our ML infra team (might be remote)

Can you:
1) propose a 60–90 minute slot with an engineer who can speak to autoscaling and GPU isolation?
2) share any pre-read on sizing assumptions we should review in advance?

Thanks — we want to have a solid agenda so we can sign off the SOW quickly.

Best,
Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Platform Engineering | Orion Biotech
(elena.morales@orionbiotech.com)


From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-04-05T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU architecture review request

Elena — great to hear. Thanks for outlining attendees. I'm looping in Sergio (solutions) and Diego (inference infra) so we have the right technical detail.

We have availability next week for a 75-minute deep-dive:
- Tue 2026-04-07 10:00–11:15 PT
- Tue 2026-04-07 15:00–16:15 PT
- Wed 2026-04-08 08:30–09:45 PT

Attached are a short slide deck that covers our Dedicated architecture and a sizing spreadsheet template we typically ask customers to fill out (capacity-sizing-spreadsheet.xlsx). If you can share a rough QPS/throughput target and expected sequence lengths across requests, Diego can pre-run some sizing options.

Proposed agenda (75m):
- 10m introductions and goals
- 20m workload profile and target SLOs (you + Arjun)
- 25m dedicated pool sizing and autoscaling behavior (Diego)
- 10m isolation and tenancy patterns (Sergio)
- 10m open questions and next steps

If one of the time slots works, I'll send a calendar invite and a passthrough for any security questionnaire you want addressed during the session.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-arch-slides.pdf, capacity-sizing-spreadsheet.xlsx

Marissa — thanks. Tue 10:00 PT conflicts with an exec review; the 15:00 PT slot would be better but Arjun has a calendar hold during that time.

Would you be able to do Mon 2026-04-06 16:00–17:15 PT instead (short notice, I know)? Or alternatively Wed 08:30 PT is preferable for Arjun. We can also shift to a 60-minute session if that helps.

For pre-reads, I'm attaching our high-level throughput goals below:
- steady-state: ~120 requests/min, avg sequence length 512 tokens
- peak bursts: ~600 requests/min for ~3–5 minute windows
- latency SLO: 95th <= 250ms for streaming outputs (where possible)
- isolation requirement: we need tenant-level isolation for regulatory reasons; multi-tenant pools acceptable only with strict network tenancy and encrypted KV cache separation

Let me know which slot you can commit to and whether Diego wants anything else ahead of time.

Best,
Elena

Hi Elena — thanks for the throughput numbers, that's really helpful. Apologies for the late reply; the Wed 08:30 PT slot works best for our engineers and gives Diego time to run a quick sizing pass (note: sent from my laptop).

To be explicit on what we'll present and what I'd like from your team before the call:
- We'll present three pool-sizing scenarios (conservative / typical / aggressive) with estimated GPU count, memory footprint, and expected p95/p99 token latency.
- Autoscaling: how our continuous batching interacts with target throughput, burst absorption windows, and cold-start behavior for KV cache-warmed instances. I'll show traces from a similar customer with bursty traffic.
- Isolation options: tenant-isolated pools (dedicated VPC + node pinning), semi-isolated pools with strict network policies, and soft multi-tenant with token- and KV-cache namespacing.

Please share before the session (if available):
- a sample request profile (json or CSV) showing sequence length distribution across requests
- expected concurrency per-tenant during peaks
- any compliance constraints (e.g., KMS/HSM, audit log retention window)

If Wed 08:30 PT is good for you, I'll send a calendar invite and include a short Loom that walks through the slides so your broader infra team can watch if they can't attend live.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime | Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
